provenance: post-hoc recount (ADR-0006: generated after protocol freeze, for artifact-release reconciliation; does not alter any frozen readout)
question: paper/freeze manifest say 1,878 added positive rows; Jul-12 retrain label cache says 1,877 (val 214 vs 215). Which is canonical and why do they differ?

verdict.cause: input drift, not counting logic: the Jul-12 pod retrain pulled features_rerank_val_R54src_F10R54.parquet from the private HF cache; that copy is a different build (26,947,531 rows, 11,933 base positive rows) than the canonical local file the frozen run used (25,283,719 rows, 12,075 base positives). One val row that flips 0->1 in the canonical pool is not flippable in the drifted copy.

recount_method: streamed the canonical local parquets, applied the exact/version corrections sidecars with the trainer's merge rule (exact_track_ids from families exact_track_request + version_duplicate_equivalence), counted rows with base label 0 and track_id in the merged target set

decomposition.note: corrects paper v11 §6 parenthetical '(five turns resolve to two catalog entries through version equivalence)' — that gloss back-derived 1878-1873=5 and coincided with the 5 version_duplicate_equivalence records in train_lt; neither explains the row arithmetic

zero_add_turns.reason: resolved track absent from the turn's candidate pool

multi_add_turns.detail: train: 14 turns add 2 rows; val: 2 turns add 2 rows, 1 turn adds 3 rows; all family exact_track_request; distinct catalog entries, not duplicate pool rows

decomposition.arithmetic: 1873 turns - 13 zero-add + 18 extra rows from multi-add = 1878
